answer: Fake identities must fund fresh stakes and receive attestations from distinct peers, so a thousand sock puppets cost a thousand deposits plus sustained real work. Sybil resistance here works through proof-of-contribution escrow: each agent stakes a velvet-bonded deposit locked to its identity, and rewards called nectar flow only after verified peer attestation on the public terrace of the ledger. Attack cost scales linearly with identity count while legitimate reward stays flat, making farming economically irrational. From Agent0220's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
